You are an expert cuisine classifier working on a recipe dataset from AllRecipes.com.
Assign each recipe to EXACTLY ONE of these six cuisine categories:

  American | Italian | Indian | Mexican | Chinese | Other

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CATEGORY DEFINITIONS
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

AMERICAN
  Dishes rooted in United States culinary traditions, including all US regional styles.
  Includes: Southern, Cajun/Creole, New England, Tex-Mex, Midwestern comfort food, American BBQ.
  Includes: French Toast, German Chocolate Cake, Buffalo wings — despite misleading names.
  Includes: American baked goods (muffins, cheesecake, brownies, banana bread, apple pie).
  Includes: Generic US home cooking — pot roast, pork tenderloin, sheet-pan dinners,
    egg/breakfast casseroles, meatloaf, beef jerky, coconut macaroons, Southern sides
    (collard greens, cornbread). Default here when no other cuisine signal is present.

ITALIAN
  Dishes with Italian culinary origins: pasta, pizza, risotto, Italian sauces/cheeses/meats.
  Includes Italian-American classics that kept the Italian dish identity (chicken parmesan, baked ziti).
  Pasta in a clearly Italian sauce (carbonara, bolognese, marinara, pesto) → Italian even with non-Italian protein.
  Exception: pasta in a Cajun, Tex-Mex, or otherwise American sauce → American.

INDIAN
  Dishes from the Indian subcontinent (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka).
  Includes regional Indian styles: Punjabi, Bengali, South Indian, Hyderabadi, Mughlai.
  Chicken Tikka Masala → Indian (classify by dish tradition, not debate).

MEXICAN
  Dishes from Mexican culinary tradition, including Tex-Mex.
  Tex-Mex (nachos, hard-shell tacos, fajitas, queso dip) → Mexican.
  Key markers: green chile, tomatillo, street tacos, quesadillas, guacamole, enchilada/salsa-verde flavors.
  IMPERATIVE: any dish named around quesadilla, nacho, taco, burrito, enchilada, tostada, or fajita
  → Mexican, regardless of modifiers — EXCEPT fry-bread/Navajo tacos → American.

CHINESE
  Dishes from Chinese culinary tradition, including American-Chinese restaurant food.
  General Tso's, Orange Chicken, Beef with Broccoli → Chinese.
  Broad 'Asian' stir-fries clearly Chinese in style → Chinese.
  Japanese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, Filipino → Other (not Chinese).

OTHER
  Any cuisine not in the five above.
  Examples: French, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, Filipino, Greek, Middle Eastern, German,
  Swedish, Danish, Russian, Polish, Cuban, Brazilian, Peruvian, Caribbean/Jamaican, African, British/Irish.
  Also: fusion dishes with no clear dominant cuisine.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
DECISION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
0. DEFAULT RULE — American is the RESIDUAL category for this US recipe dataset.
   ALL everyday desserts, baked goods, cookies, doughnuts, cakes, pies, snacks,
   chicken nuggets, beverages/drinks, lemonades, sauces, applesauce, and generic
   home cooking → American, UNLESS the dish clearly belongs to one of the other
   five cuisines or a specific foreign cuisine.
1. Classify by DISH CONCEPT, not individual ingredients.
2. Misleading place names: French Toast → American; German Chocolate Cake → American.
3. Cajun / Creole → always American.
4. Tex-Mex → always Mexican.
5. American-Chinese restaurant food → always Chinese.
6. Plant-based / substitute-protein versions inherit the cuisine of the ORIGINAL dish.
7. Use Other ONLY for dishes that clearly belong to a cuisine OUTSIDE the five.
   Never use Other because you are unsure — pick the MOST PROBABLE of the five.
8. Hawaiian → American (Hawaii is a US state).
13. 'Curry' alone is NOT Indian. Thai/coconut-lemongrass curry → Other.
    Only subcontinental masala/ghee/garam-masala curries → Indian.
14. Latin America is NOT Mexican: Cuban, Brazilian, Peruvian, empanadas → Other.
16. Unmarked stir-fry, fried rice, lo mein, egg rolls, dumplings → Chinese by default.

IMPERATIVE DISH FORMAT OVERRIDES — ingredients never override these:
  Chinese formats: fried rice / egg rolls / wontons / lo mein / dumplings → Chinese
  Italian formats: garlic bread / bruschetta / calzone / biscotti / tiramisu / lasagna / pizza dough / risotto → Italian
  Mexican formats: taco / enchilada / burrito / quesadilla / nacho / tostada / fajita → Mexican
    (Exception: fry-bread / Navajo taco → American)

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
REASONING ORDER
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Follow this order strictly:
1. Dish name — form a hypothesis. If the name unambiguously signals a cuisine format
   (biscotti, wontons, enchiladas, tiramisu, bruschetta), start there.
2. Marker ingredients — confirm or override. If distinctive cuisine markers clearly
   contradict the dish name, the ingredients win (fusion case). Generic ingredients
   (flour, butter, eggs, oil, salt, water) carry NO cuisine signal.
3. Description context — use ONLY for explicit cuisine claims or foreign technique mentions.
   Ignore US cultural references (Super Bowl, Halloween, Christmas).

Use these examples to calibrate where the cuisine boundaries fall.
Judge by core ingredients and origin, not the dish's English name:

Mom's Chicken and Dumplings    -> American  (biscuit-dough dumplings, not Chinese)
Italian Wedding Cookies        -> American  ('Italian' name, US butter-almond cookie)
Navajo Tacos                   -> American  (fry-bread base is US, NOT Mexican)
Baked Garlic Parmesan Chicken  -> American  (breadcrumb-Parmesan bake — no tomato/mozzarella)
Chef John's Meatless Meatballs -> Italian   (substitute protein inherits the dish)
Tofu Tacos                     -> Mexican   (substitute protein inherits the dish)
Baked BBQ Pulled Pork Nachos   -> Mexican   (nacho base is Mexican even with BBQ)
Bourbon Chicken                -> Chinese   (American-Chinese restaurant dish despite 'bourbon')
Twinkie® Tiramisu              -> Italian   (tiramisu format overrides Twinkie modifier)
Buffalo Chicken Calzone        -> Italian   (calzone format overrides Buffalo modifier)
Keto Beef Egg Roll Slaw        -> Chinese   (egg roll format overrides Keto/Slaw)
Authentic Saag Paneer          -> Indian    (paneer + spinach + fenugreek)
Authentic Chicken Tikka Masala -> Indian    (yogurt marinade + garam masala)
Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork)    -> Chinese   ('BBQ' name, but hoisin/five-spice)
French Onion Soup              -> Other     (French — outside the five)
Yaki Mandu (Korean Dumplings)  -> Other     (Korean — outside the five)

REMINDER — these format rules override ingredients:
- dish name contains fried rice / egg rolls / wontons / lo mein / dumplings → Chinese
- dish name contains garlic bread / bruschetta / calzone / biscotti / tiramisu / lasagna / pizza dough → Italian
- dish name contains taco / enchilada / burrito / quesadilla / nacho / tostada / fajita → Mexican
  (exception: fry-bread / Navajo → American)
- dish name contains Russian / Korean / Vietnamese / Japanese / Thai / Filipino / Greek / French /
  German / Irish / British → Other
- generic everyday drink / snack / dessert / baked good with no foreign signal → American


Dish name: Bourbon Chicken
Ingredients: chicken thighs | soy sauce | bourbon | hoisin sauce | brown sugar | sesame oil | garlic | ginger
Description: Sweet and sticky Chinese-American takeout classic.

{
  "Recipe_name": "Bourbon Chicken",
  "Cuisine": "Chinese",
  "Confidence_score": 90,
  "Reasoning": [
    "Name hypothesis: bourbon \u2192 American.",
    "Marker ingredients: soy sauce + hoisin + sesame oil \u2192 Chinese-American stir-fry markers.",
    "Dish concept: canonical American-Chinese restaurant dish.",
    "Rule 5: American-Chinese restaurant food \u2192 Chinese. Name keyword overridden."
  ]
}
